subject: Materials Science
title: Edge Dislocations: The Extra Half-Plane
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Edge Dislocations: The Extra Half-Plane.

hook.text: Bend a paperclip and it stays bent. That permanent deformation happens atom by atom along a line.

buildup.text: An edge dislocation is an extra half-plane of atoms inserted into the crystal lattice.

discovery.text: When stress is applied, the dislocation glides one atomic step at a time — far less force than moving an entire plane.

twist.text: Without dislocations, metals would need 1,000 times more stress to deform — they'd be nearly unworkable.

climax.text: Every hammer strike, every car panel press moves billions of dislocations through the metal.

punchline.text: Metals bend because atoms slip, one row at a time, along a defect line.

quiz.question: Why do dislocations make metals easier to deform?
options: They remove atoms, making the metal lighter
They allow slip one row at a time instead of moving an entire plane
They melt the metal locally at the defect
